candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

questionnaire.text: What experience do you have supporting adolescents, families, or individuals receiving behavioral health services?
questionnaire.response:
In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I waited for my son and daughter to be eligible for preK and kindergarten so I could return to work.   I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English.  During those 9 years I learned not only to help many Spanish speaking students learn English, but how to care for the ones who were emotionally distressed from various personal problems at home, I would accompany them to the social workers office and translate all the problems they were experiencing at home. I realized how much suffering and empathy was needed for my role.  I later left the position to care for my son who had a massive brain tumor and barely survived during the surgery.  As my son, progressed and I was forced to stay home.  I found work on line, which happened to be during COVID. 
   I recently went back to work part time as a Substitute teacher, and still find myself helping students of all ages with a variety of emotional issues.

work_history.title: Clinical Director
work_history.summary: Provide clinical leadership and oversight for behavioral health and substance use treatment services, supporting the delivery of safe, ethical, evidence-based, and recovery-oriented care. Provide clinical oversight and leadership for treatment services, ensuring clinical programming is implemented consistently and aligns with organizational, licensing, and accreditation requirements. Conduct comprehensive clinical assessments and determine appropriate ASAM level of care and treatment placement based on presenting needs, risk factors, withdrawal concerns, mental health symptoms, and recovery environment. Support clinical staff with diagnostic formulation, treatment planning, clinical interventions, documentation, and ongoing evaluation of client progress. Provide individual and group clinical supervision, case consultation, mentoring, and professional development to counselors and other assigned staff. Facilitate interdisciplinary treatment team meetings and clinical case consultations to promote coordinated, clinically appropriate care. Review clinical documentation and provide feedback regarding assessment quality, treatment plans, progress notes, group documentation, and continuity of care. Promote the integration of evidence-based practices, trauma-informed care, motivational interviewing, client-centered interventions, and recovery-oriented approaches throughout clinical programming. Monitor the delivery of daily clinical programming and address barriers affecting treatment quality, staff performance, client engagement, and continuity of care. Assist facility leadership with program development, clinical process improvement, staff training, and implementation of new services. Support compliance with applicable NC DHHS regulations, CARF standards, ASAM Criteria, organizational policies, and clinical documentation requirements. Maintain a safe, structured, therapeutic environment and provide or coordinate crisis intervention and clinical response when indicated. Collaborate with medical, behavioral health, nursing, case management, and facility leadership teams to address complex client needs and promote continuity of care. Advocate for clients and incorporate client-centered perspectives into treatment planning, discharge planning, and recovery goals. Maintain accurate and timely clinical records and ensure completion of required documentation, training, and compliance activities.

Dear Hiring Manager,
I am writing to express my interest in joining your organization. With a career in healthcare spanning more than 25 years, beginning in 1998 as a Unit Secretary and progressing to Clinic Administrator II, I have developed a strong foundation in healthcare operations, team leadership, staff development, and clinic management. Throughout my career, I have remained committed to supporting both the people who deliver care and the patients who depend on it.

Re: Primary Therapist Position

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position at Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) in Boca Raton, Florida. With a Ph.D. in Counselor Education and Supervision, a master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, and experience in clinical practice, counselor education, and clinical training, I bring an integrated perspective on mental health care that combines evidence-informed clinical approaches, developmental knowledge, multicultural awareness, and a commitment to supporting individuals through challenging life transitions. Having recently relocated back to Florida from Connecticut, I am currently working toward full licensure with the State of Florida and practicing as a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI). I am also legally authorized to live and work in the United States without employer sponsorship. I am particularly interested in AWA’s work with adolescents and its emphasis on individualized, collaborative care that supports emotional well-being, resilience, and personal growth, and I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to AWA’s work with adolescents and families from diverse backgrounds.

As a Portuguese-English bilingual professional with Spanish skills, I bring a multicultural perspective that supports my commitment to culturally responsive and accessible mental health care. My Brazilian background and international experience have shaped my appreciation for the ways culture, identity, family expectations, and transitions influence individuals’ experiences and help-seeking behaviors. I recognize the importance of building therapeutic relationships that honor clients’ culture and lived experiences while fostering trust, collaboration, and respect. 

My clinical experience and interests include working with concerns such as anxiety, depression, trauma, substance use/abuse, domestic violence, acculturation, relationship difficulties, and life transitions. My therapeutic approach reflects evidence-informed assimilative integration, grounded primarily in Narrative Therapy and Relational-Cultural Theory (RCT), while incorporating complementary approaches such as Solution-Focused Brief Therapy (SFBT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and Motivational Interviewing (MI) to meet clients’ unique needs and therapeutic goals. I strive to create a warm, collaborative, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment in which clients can explore their experiences, identify strengths, develop effective coping strategies, and work toward meaningful goals. My approach is grounded in cultural humility, trauma-responsive care, and an understanding of how relationships, family systems, cultural contexts, and broader social factors influence mental health and development.

I have a particular interest in human development across the lifespan, which is reflected in both my clinical work and my teaching. As an instructor, I have taught Lifespan and Human Development to counseling students, a course that deepens my engagement with developmental theories and how biological, psychological, social, cultural, and relational factors shape individuals’ experiences and well-being at different stages of life. This academic focus complements my interest in working with adolescents and understanding the unique developmental, emotional, interpersonal, and family-related challenges they may experience. I value developmentally responsive, trauma-informed, and strengths-based approaches that recognize each young person’s needs while engaging families and other members of the treatment team to support growth, resilience, and emotional well-being.

My clinical background also includes experience with individuals with autism and intellectual disabilities. In Brazil, I developed a project focused on social inclusion and group counseling for individuals with developmental disabilities, which gave me valuable experience understanding and addressing social, interpersonal, developmental, and emotional needs. This experience strengthened my commitment to adapting support to individuals’ unique circumstances and fostering environments that promote inclusion, connection, and personal growth. My background in career counseling further strengthened my experience supporting young individuals as they navigate transitions, develop self-awareness, and identify meaningful paths forward.

In addition to my clinical work, I served as an Assistant Professor of Practice and Clinical Training Director at Fairfield University in Connecticut, where I taught and mentored counseling students, coordinated clinical placements, collaborated with clinical supervisors and community partners, and supported students’ professional development. My responsibilities included coordinating field placements, communicating with supervisors and training sites, and helping students connect academic knowledge with clinical practice. This experience strengthened my ability to respectfully collaborate across professional roles, communicate effectively, maintain organized documentation, and appreciate the importance of coordinated care and professional accountability. My teaching experience in counseling skills, advanced treatment and counseling interventions, group work, ethics, career counseling, and human development also informs my understanding of therapeutic relationships, treatment planning, and the importance of adapting interventions to clients’ developmental and contextual needs.

I believe I am drawn to AWA’s multidisciplinary treatment environment and the opportunity to collaborate with therapists, psychiatrists, and other clinical professionals to support adolescents’ mental health and well-being. I value comprehensive, individualized treatment that integrates assessment, collaborative goal setting, therapeutic interventions, ongoing progress evaluation, family engagement, and continuity of care. I also recognize the importance of timely, accurate clinical documentation, ethical practice, appropriate consultation, and coordination with the treatment team to promote effective, consistent care.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, expertise in counselor education and human development, multicultural perspective, and commitment to accessible, trauma-responsive, strengths-based, and evidence-informed care could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and the adolescents and families it serves.

Sincerely,

Paula Lazarim, Ph.D., M.S., NCC
Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern

Tiandra Arnold
6514 Croydon Cove
Memphis, TN 38141
(901) 236-2412 | tiandra97@gmail.com

October 20, 2026

Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am happy to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a professional background in behavioral health intake, clinical counseling, healthcare administration, and client services, I bring a unique combination of clinical understanding, organizational skills, and compassionate communication that aligns with the responsibilities of this role.

Throughout my career, I have gained valuable experience supporting individuals and families navigating behavioral health services. In my previous role as a Mental Health Intake Assessor at Crestwyn Behavioral Health, I developed experience conducting assessments, gathering clinical information, identifying presenting concerns, and supporting individuals through the initial stages of accessing mental health treatment. This experience strengthened my ability to communicate effectively with individuals experiencing emotional distress while maintaining professionalism, empathy, and attention to detail.

Currently, I serve as a Team Lead and clinician within a behavioral health private practice, where my responsibilities extend beyond direct client care to include insurance verification, billing coordination, client communication, administrative support, and training graduate-level interns. In this role, I regularly navigate sensitive client concerns, coordinate services, maintain accurate documentation, and collaborate with team members to ensure efficient daily operations. Dear Hiring Team,

I’m excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. My background in digital healthcare, patient support, and healthcare operations has taught me how important it is to meet people with compassion, communicate clearly during stressful situations, and help them navigate the next steps toward getting the care they need.

At Twentyeight Health, I supported patients with prescription access, insurance-related barriers, pharmacy coordination, and other sensitive healthcare concerns in a fully remote environment. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can feel overwhelming, and I would approach each interaction with patience, respect, and a nonjudgmental attitude. I would take seriously the responsibility of helping individuals and families understand their options and move toward an appropriate next step.

I’m particularly interested in this opportunity because it combines compassionate patient communication with the coordination, documentation, and follow-through that have been central to my previous roles. I also bring substantial remote-work experience and a proactive approach to managing my workload independently, while recognizing when collaboration or escalation is needed.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my healthcare support experience, attention to detail, and commitment to compassionate care could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Brittany Luman

TONI D COLE
(573) 220- 2647            toni.d.cole@gmail.com            Montgomery City, MO  63361

To Adolescent Wellness Academy,

I am a detail-oriented professional praised as creative, flexible, and compassionate. I excel in working in self-driven positions. I have worked with people with disabilities, at-risk, and their families while assessing behavior and providing crisis intervention, where my approach is to first seek to understand. I have experience with a broad range of disability and mental health diagnoses of varying ages, recognizing that each person’s character and nuances influence their lives.

I have advocated and provided support in-person across all socio-economic levels and environments - home, school, work, and communities. I learned and honed my foundational knowledge and skills with the Judevine Center for Autism, where I first became aware of the necessity and benefit of observing with all my senses, trial and error, adaptation, and setting up for success. These skills were vital as I have moved through various positions, understanding early in my career how to approach each situation and person in ways that met with their unique personality and needs, utilizing ABA, Collaborative & Prevention Solutions (CPS), and other effective approaches.

I have been certified and provided suicide prevention training and direct practice with people in crisis, especially when the crisis was often not seen visually but understood deeply when considering personal and environmental stressors.  I have authored and facilitated curriculums for those with disabilities and at-risk, families, support staff, and educators. At Willows Way, I designed the Project HEART program with the approach - learning happens best while having fun. Project HEART reached the three-year grant goal in the first year of programming, earned the MACDDS “Cutting Edge” award, and secured on-going funding through the Developmental Disabilities Resource Board (DDRB) of St. Charles County. At the eleventh hour, I was also placed in charge of navigating the closing of a day program and beginning a new one, now called RISE. I was commended for the smooth and successful transition, as well as developing a promising new program format. Both Project HEART and RISE continue to operate under the frameworks I created.

I left employment six years ago to support my teenage son through debilitating anxiety. He is diagnosed with ASD – Pathological Demand Avoidance (PDA) profile. My years working with and around “behavior” resulted in a deep passion for us to begin viewing and approaching behavior as communication of something I don’t yet understand, or know, what will be most helpful for this person. Too often only a diagnosis is what is seen, not the person who is trying to navigate the complexities of the diagnosis from their unique experiences, perspective, and resources.  I believe working as a team, focused on understanding the person first, is where the greatest opportunities exist to help people better navigate their world now and in the future.

I look forward to sharing more of how I am a uniquely qualified candidate to serve patients and their families as a remote Admissions Coordinator.

Sincerely,

TONI D. COLE

Dear Hiring Team,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With an M.Sc. in Psychology and experience working with individuals across different age groups, I bring a strong foundation in mental health, client communication, empathetic engagement, and coordinating support for individuals and families navigating psychological challenges.

My professional experience includes providing online therapy sessions for adults, working as a child-parent consultant, and supporting children with diverse developmental and behavioural needs. These roles have strengthened my ability to communicate sensitively with clients and caregivers, understand individual concerns, establish rapport, and help people identify appropriate next steps for their mental health needs. My therapeutic background includes CBT, REBT, DBT, arts-based therapy, and trauma-informed approaches, which has further developed my understanding of the importance of compassionate, person-centred care.

Dear Adolescent Wellness Hiring Team,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness. With previous experience working as a Mental Health Technician at Purchase Youth Village in Benton, Kentucky, along with my background in healthcare administration and medical billing, I believe I can bring a valuable combination of compassion, communication skills, and organizational experience to your team.

During my time at Purchase Youth Village, I gained hands-on experience working with youth experiencing mental health and behavioral challenges. This experience strengthened my understanding of the importance of patience, empathy, safety, and providing support in a structured treatment environment. I understand that seeking mental health treatment can be an overwhelming experience for adolescents and their families, and I would value the opportunity to help make the admissions process more approachable and supportive.

In my current or previous healthcare administrative work with Valor Health, I have developed experience navigating insurance processes, communicating with insurance providers, resolving billing issues, and helping address coverage concerns. These responsibilities have strengthened my attention to detail, problem-solving abilities, and understanding of the administrative side of healthcare. I believe these skills would translate well to coordinating admissions, communicating with families, and helping individuals navigate the steps toward receiving care.

I am passionate about the importance of mental health support for adolescents and would welcome the opportunity to combine my direct-care experience with my healthcare administrative background to contribute to Adolescent Wellness. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and skills could benefit your team.

Sincerely,

Makayla Wadkins

Hiring Manager

Re: Employment Opportunity

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to express my interest in joining the team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a Bachelor of Science in Public Health, specializing in Health Promotion and Education from Kent State University, along with professional experience in healthcare support, customer service, and management, I believe I would bring compassion, dedication, and valuable skills to your organization.

Throughout my professional career, I have developed strong communication, problem-solving, organizational, and interpersonal skills. My experience with Public Consulting Group allowed me to assist individuals navigating complex healthcare systems, maintain accurate documentation, address concerns, and provide compassionate support while meeting organizational expectations.

I am particularly drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy because of my passion for mental health awareness, behavioral health, and helping young people overcome challenges while developing confidence, resilience, and healthy coping skills. I understand the importance of creating a supportive, structured, and judgment-free environment where adolescents feel heard, respected, and empowered.

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. As a bilingual English and Spanish professional with experience supporting individuals from diverse backgrounds, providing customer service, handling documentation, and maintaining confidentiality in an educational setting, I bring a compassionate, organized, and service-oriented approach to helping people navigate important processes. I am especially drawn to this opportunity because it combines meaningful client support with clear communication, careful coordination, and the opportunity to help individuals and families take the first step toward receiving the care they need.

Through my experience working in the Accessibility Services Office at California State University, East Bay, I developed a strong understanding of the importance of patience, empathy, discretion, and respectful communication. I supported students with diverse needs, assisted with check-in procedures, helped explain confidentiality forms, and reviewed schedules and online documents. These responsibilities taught me to listen carefully, communicate information clearly, respect sensitive information, and approach each interaction with professionalism and understanding. I recognize that people seeking mental health or substance use treatment may be experiencing uncertainty, fear, or stress, and I would approach every conversation with compassion, dignity, and a commitment to helping them understand their next steps.

As a bilingual English and Spanish speaker, I can bring an additional communication strength to interactions with clients and families from different backgrounds. I understand how important it is for people to feel heard, respected, and comfortable asking questions, particularly when navigating an unfamiliar or emotionally challenging process. I would strive to communicate in clear, accessible language, explain available next steps within established guidelines, and help callers feel supported rather than overwhelmed. I would also approach every interaction with cultural awareness and respect for each person's individual circumstances.

I also bring strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple responsibilities while maintaining accurate information. My experience reviewing student schedules and documents has reinforced the importance of careful recordkeeping, confidentiality, and following established procedures. I am comfortable communicating virtually and using digital tools to review information and support documentation. I would bring this same care and consistency to tracking inquiries, following up with prospective clients and families, coordinating assessments and appointments, and helping ensure that information is documented accurately. I am eager to learn the organization's specific CRM and electronic medical record systems, admissions procedures, and insurance verification workflows.

What particularly motivates me about this opportunity is the chance to make a meaningful difference before a client even begins treatment. A first phone call can be an important moment for someone seeking help, and I would take that responsibility seriously. I would aim to be a calm, welcoming, and dependable point of contact while respecting privacy, following established protocols, and ensuring that callers receive clear information about the appropriate next steps. I would also remain mindful of the importance of timely follow-up, collaboration with the admissions team, and connecting callers with the appropriate resources when a program is not the right fit.

As a first-generation college graduate, I value the importance of access, encouragement, and supportive guidance when navigating unfamiliar systems. I would bring that perspective, along with my bilingual communication skills, adaptability, and genuine desire to help others, to the admissions team. I am enthusiastic about the opportunity to contribute to an organization dedicated to helping individuals and families take meaningful steps toward mental health and recovery.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my communication skills, administrative experience, and compassionate approach could contribute to the Virtual Admissions Coordinator team. Dear Hiring Team,
I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. I recently graduated from the University of California, San Diego, with a Bachelor of Science in Education Sciences and a Bachelor of Arts in Human Developmental Sciences. With a strong interest in counseling and mental health, I am excited about the opportunity to support individuals and families seeking treatment and guidance.
For over three years, I worked at UC San Diego's Early Childhood Education Center, where I supported young children, collaborated with educators, and developed strong communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills. Additionally, I completed an occupational therapy internship in a treatment setting serving adolescents experiencing mental health challenges. This experience strengthened my interest in behavioral health and taught me the importance of patience, empathy, and individualized support.
Although my professional experience has primarily been in education and direct support, I am eager to expand my skills into behavioral health admissions and care coordination. As someone who is bilingual in English and Spanish, I value the importance of clear, compassionate communication, especially when helping individuals and families navigate unfamiliar or challenging situations. I am organized, adaptable, and eager to learn new systems and procedures.
I would appreciate the opportunity to contribute to your team while continuing to grow professionally in the mental health field. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss my qualifications further.
Sincerely,
Ariday Rubio

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a Bachelor's degree in Psychology, extensive experience working with youth and families, and a strong passion for supporting individuals through challenging life transitions, I am confident I would bring empathy, professionalism, and dedication to your admissions team.

Throughout my career, I have worked in roles that required building trust, communicating with diverse populations, maintaining confidentiality, and guiding individuals through important decisions. As a substitute teacher supporting both general education and special needs students, I regularly serve as a calm and reassuring presence for students and families navigating emotional, behavioral, and academic challenges. These experiences have strengthened my ability to listen actively, assess needs, and respond with compassion while maintaining clear and professional communication.

In addition to my educational background, I am an entrepreneur and business owner who independently manages client relationships, scheduling, documentation, follow-up communications, and administrative processes. This experience has sharpened my organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to effectively manage multiple priorities in a remote and self-directed environment.

What draws me most to this opportunity is the chance to be the first point of contact for individuals and families seeking support. I understand that reaching out for help often requires courage, and I am committed to ensuring every caller feels heard, respected, and guided toward the appropriate next step. My background in psychology gives me a strong understanding of mental health challenges, while my professional experiences have taught me how to communicate sensitive information with empathy and professionalism.

I am particularly inspired by the missions of Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center and the commitment both organizations demonstrate toward helping individuals and families heal. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my communication skills, client-focused approach, and passion for behavioral health to your growing team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background, skills, and commitment to helping others align with the needs of your organization.

candidates.summary:
I have a strong background in behavioral health, healthcare operations, patient coordination, intake, admissions, and clinical support. Most recently, I worked as a Front of House Supervisor at Relive Health, where I supported day-to-day clinic operations, coordinated scheduling, provider communication, treatment follow-up, bloodwork, client education, documentation, payments, and overall patient flow. I also helped maintain clinic workflows and served as a primary point of contact between clients, providers, and clinical staff.

Prior to that, I worked at Austin Oaks Hospital, an inpatient psychiatric facility, in reception and intake. In that role, I supported the admissions process by gathering demographic and clinical information, coordinating assessments, verifying insurance benefits and authorization requirements, preparing admission and consent documentation, maintaining confidential records, communicating with patients and families, and working closely with clinical staff and outside referral sources. This experience gave me extensive exposure to behavioral health, crisis situations, sensitive patient communication, and the importance of accuracy and compassion during the intake process.

I also worked as a Patient Observation Assistant with Ascension Seton, where I provided continuous one-on-one observation for high-risk patients across multiple hospital settings. I monitored patient safety, documented observations, communicated changes or concerns to nursing staff, followed safety protocols, and supported patients experiencing behavioral health crises, confusion, suicide risk, or other safety concerns.

Earlier in my career, I worked at Walgreens in both customer service and pharmacy support, where I gained additional experience with healthcare communication, confidentiality, medication-related workflows, patient information, and fast-paced customer service.

Across these roles, I have developed strong skills in patient advocacy, behavioral health, intake and admissions, care coordination, scheduling, documentation, HIPAA compliance, insurance verification, crisis communication, provider coordination, and healthcare operations. I am highly organized, comfortable managing multiple priorities, and experienced in working with patients and families during stressful or sensitive situations. I am also completing my Bachelor of Science in Psychology at The University of Texas at Austin, which has further strengthened my understanding of mental health, human behavior, and patient-centered care. My combination of behavioral health experience, clinical operations experience, and psychology education is what makes me especially interested in continuing my career in adolescent mental health and clinical coordination.

work_history.title: Front of House Supervisor
work_history.summary: Manage day-to-day clinic and client operations for a medical wellness and aesthetics clinic, serving as a primary point of contact and client advocate throughout the client journey from initial inquiry and consultation through treatment and ongoing follow-up. Serve as a liaison between clients, providers, and clinical staff by assisting with individualized treatment plans, coordinating recommended services, addressing client needs and concerns, tracking treatment progress, and maintaining ongoing communication to support treatment adherence and continuity of care. Conduct and support wellness and aesthetic consultations, educating prospective and existing clients on treatment options, pricing, memberships, and next steps across medical weight loss, hormone optimization, peptide therapy, wellness, and aesthetic services. Manage client outreach and lead follow-up, including prospective client engagement, appointment conversion, treatment follow-ups, re-engagement, appointment confirmations, and ongoing relationship management. Coordinate bloodwork, provider consultations, treatment appointments, recurring therapies, and follow-up visits while communicating between clients, providers, and clinical staff to ensure timely progression through treatment. Support aesthetic and wellness treatment operations by coordinating client preparation, treatment scheduling, provider availability, room utilization, and post-consultation follow-up. Help establish and maintain clinic workflows and operational processes, including scheduling procedures, client communication, treatment coordination, documentation, membership management, and front-office organization. Maintain accurate client records, treatment information, financial accounts, memberships, and confidential health information in accordance with HIPAA requirements while processing payments and providing billing support. Work closely with providers, leadership, and clinical staff to advocate for client needs, resolve concerns, facilitate treatment recommendations and follow-up, accommodate scheduling needs, and maintain an organized and high-quality client experience.

work_history.title: Receptionist AND Intake Assistant
work_history.summary: Serve as the primary front-desk and intake point of contact for an 80-bed inpatient psychiatric facility, managing high-volume telephone and in-person communication with patients, families, providers, and external agencies. Prepare and review admission and consent documentation, collect demographic and clinical information, and maintain accurate records in accordance with hospital policies and HIPAA requirements. Maintain daily census reports and admissions documentation supporting hospital intake operations and reporting requirements.

Participated in clinical handoffs to ensure continuity of observation and communication of pertinent patient behaviors and safety concerns.

My professional experience includes approximately two and a half years working at the City Mission, where I supported individuals experiencing homelessness and facing challenging life circumstances. This experience strengthened my ability to connect with people from diverse backgrounds, recognize the barriers they face, and approach each individual with compassion, patience, and respect. My lived experience in recovery has given me a personal understanding of the challenges involved in overcoming substance use and making lasting changes. I know that recovery is not always a straight path, and I understand the importance of meeting people where they are without judgment. I believe that sharing hope, building trust, encouraging personal responsibility, and helping individuals connect with appropriate resources can make a meaningful difference in their recovery journey.

Along with my lived experience, my PRSS background and Community Health Worker certification provide a foundation for supporting individuals as they navigate recovery, access community resources, and work toward greater independence. I am committed to maintaining professional boundaries, respecting each person’s dignity, and supporting recovery goals that are meaningful to the individual. I bring a strong work ethic, a willingness to learn, and a genuine desire to help others recognize their own strengths and potential.

I am seeking an opportunity to combine my professional skills and personal perspective to make a positive impact within an organization dedicated to recovery and behavioral health. My goal is to help others receive the encouragement, support, and opportunities they need to build a better future, while continuing to grow as a recovery professional.

Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience, qualifications, and commitment to helping others could contribute to your team and the individuals you serve. I look forward to the possibility of working together to make a meaningful difference in our community.

Sincerely,
Brandon Belt

candidates.cover_letter:
I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a professional background in human services, case management, crisis intervention, and emergency management; I have developed a strong commitment to helping individuals and families navigate challenging circumstances and connect with the support and resources they need.

In my experience as a remote crisis responder, I have independently managed incoming calls, completed documentation, maintained follow-ups, and coordinated services while working with individuals experiencing difficult and often stressful situations. My remote work experience has strengthened my ability to manage competing priorities, maintain an organized workflow, exercise sound judgment, and ensure that responsibilities are completed accurately and promptly without requiring constant supervision.

Additionally, my background includes conducting assessments, coordinating referrals, and connecting clients with appropriate treatment services and community resources. These responsibilities have strengthened my ability to identify individual needs, communicate options clearly, and help clients navigate the process of accessing care. I understand the importance of timely follow-through, accurate recordkeeping, confidentiality, and professional communication when managing sensitive client information.

I recognize that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an emotional and overwhelming experience for individuals and their families. I would approach every interaction with empathy, patience, and professionalism while helping callers understand their options and determine the appropriate next steps. My crisis response experience has taught me the importance of listening without judgment, building trust quickly, and providing clear guidance during vulnerable moments.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because both Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center are committed to helping individuals access behavioral health and recovery services. I would welcome the opportunity to apply my experience in crisis response, assessment, referral coordination, and remote service delivery to support the admissions process, maintain consistent communication with prospective clients and referral sources, and help individuals and families connect with the appropriate level of care.

I am confident that my human services background, independent remote work experience, strong organizational skills, and dedication to compassionate client care would make me a valuable addition to your team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications and commitment to helping others align with the needs of Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Sincerely,

Sherell Johnson

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With experience in behavioral health admissions and intake, remote work, trauma-informed care, and client coordination, I offer the combination of compassion, professionalism, and organizational skills needed to support individuals and families seeking treatment.

Throughout my career, I have developed a strong understanding of how important the first interaction can be for someone reaching out for help. My admissions and intake experience has prepared me to communicate with individuals during vulnerable moments, gather sensitive information, assess their needs, and help guide them toward appropriate services. I understand the importance of making every caller feel heard, respected, and supported while ensuring that the admissions process moves forward efficiently.

In my current role as a Direct Support Professional with Service Alternatives, I support foster youth experiencing behavioral, emotional, and developmental challenges. I work closely with families, caregivers, and multidisciplinary teams to coordinate care, maintain confidential records, manage appointments, and respond calmly to challenging situations. This experience has strengthened my ability to communicate with empathy while remaining focused on practical solutions.

My previous experience with the Washington Department of Health further developed my skills in telephone outreach, sensitive documentation, resource coordination, and helping individuals navigate stressful circumstances. Additionally, my remote work experience has equipped me with the independence, accountability, time management, and communication skills necessary to remain productive and organized without constant supervision.

I am comfortable working with electronic records, maintaining confidentiality, managing multiple priorities, and following through to ensure individuals receive the assistance they need. I recognize that successful admissions coordination requires more than scheduling appointments. It requires building trust, removing barriers, maintaining consistent communication, and helping people take that important first step toward recovery.

What excites me most about this opportunity is the ability to combine my professional experience with my genuine passion for helping people. I would be proud to represent both Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center as a compassionate and dependable first point of contact.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, dedication, and commitment to quality care would make me a valuable addition to your admissions team.

Thank you,
Jessica Avery

candidates.cover_letter:
Allison Bertolino
Port Saint Lucie, FL 34983

October 20, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescence Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining Adolescence Wellness Academy. With over three years of experience in behavioral health admissions, client assessments, insurance verification, treatment coordination, and patient intake, I have developed a strong understanding of the importance of compassionate, efficient, and individualized care. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, professionalism, and dedication to your team and contribute to helping adolescents and their families access the support and treatment they need.

In my current role as Lead Day Time Admissions Coordinator at Archstone Behavioral Health, I oversee the admissions process from the initial inquiry through enrollment. My responsibilities include verifying insurance benefits, conducting comprehensive assessments and screenings, identifying potential substance use disorders, and helping determine appropriate levels of care. I also coordinate travel arrangements, maintain accurate and confidential client records, and collaborate with probation officers and court officials when coordinating mandated treatment services. These responsibilities have strengthened my ability to manage competing priorities, communicate effectively with individuals and families during difficult circumstances, and ensure a smooth and supportive admissions experience.

My previous experience as an Admissions Coordinator with Magnolia Ranch Recovery and Genesis Detox further developed my skills in client communication, treatment coordination, documentation, and collaboration with multidisciplinary teams to support individualized treatment planning. In addition, my experience as a Customer Service Manager strengthened my leadership, problem-solving, organization, and conflict-resolution skills. I understand the importance of building trust, responding to concerns with empathy, maintaining confidentiality, and helping people navigate what can often be an overwhelming process.

I believe my combination of behavioral health admissions experience, strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and compassionate approach would make me a valuable addition to Adolescence Wellness Academy. I am especially interested in the opportunity to apply my experience in a setting focused on supporting adolescents and their families, where clear communication, patience, and a commitment to quality care are essential.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background, skills, and dedication to behavioral health can contribute to the mission of Adolescence Wellness Academy. I look forward to the possibility of speaking with you.

Sincerely,
Allison Bertolino

October 20, 2026  

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinators position with Adolescent Wellness Academy.  I have always had a passion for helping others, especially individuals and families going through difficult situations. With my bachelor’s degree in psychology and my experience in crisis intervention, case management, and healthcare, I believe I have developed the skills necessary to provide compassionate and professional support to individuals seeking mental health treatment.
During my time as a Mobile Crisis Worker at Hill Country MHDD in Kerrville, Texas, I worked directly with individuals experiencing mental health crises. My responsibilities included conducting crisis assessments, evaluating suicidal or homicidal thoughts and plans, providing immediate crisis intervention, and developing appropriate safety plans. I also collaborated with Licensed Practitioners (LPHAs) to discuss my assessments and determine the appropriate next steps, including whether an individual needed inpatient hospitalization or could safely return home with a safety plan.
An important part of my role also involved communicating directly with family members to better understand the individual’s situation. I would ask questions to gather additional information, discuss their concerns, and help determine what support was available at home. Through these experiences, I learned how important it is to build trust, listen without judgment, and help families feel supported when making difficult decisions.  I am also bilingual in English and Spanish, allowing me to communicate with and support individuals and families from different backgrounds.

What interests me most about this opportunity is being able to make a difference from the very first conversation. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be overwhelming, especially for parents who are concerned about their children and may not know where to begin. I would love the opportunity to help guide families through the admissions process while providing reassurance, understanding, and compassion during a difficult time in their lives.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to bring my experience, dedication, and passion for helping others to Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,

Clarissa Mata

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,
When someone calls on one of the hardest days of their life, they need a calm, clear, compassionate voice that can move them from overwhelm to a concrete next step. That is exactly the kind of work I am built for, and it is why I am applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator role supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.
I hold a Bachelor’s degree in Applied Childhood Psychology and am currently enrolled in Liberty University’s Master of Social Work program with a focus on individual and family clinical practice. My studies have deepened my understanding of adolescent mental health, family systems, trauma, and the barriers families face when they try to access care. Outside the classroom, I have spent years supporting children and families directly, as a nanny, youth coach, and through administrative work that regularly involved speaking with parents under stress. At RVJ, I managed parent and player calls for sports programs, navigating questions, concerns, and scheduling with patience and follow-through. As a Store Manager at Kirkland’s, I led a sales team, tracked performance in CRM systems, and consistently followed up until issues were resolved. Those roles taught me how to manage a pipeline independently, document accurately, and stay organized without daily oversight—skills that translate directly to remote admissions work.
I am especially drawn to the dual focus of AWA and PRC. Supporting teens ages 13–17 and their families through PHP and IOP aligns closely with my background and with why I am pursuing social work: to be a steady, practical advocate for young people and families navigating instability. At the same time, I am comfortable discussing substance use treatment and co-occurring conditions with adults and their loved ones. I understand that the first conversation is often the hardest one, and I bring a warm, confident phone presence along with the discipline to verify insurance, coordinate assessments and intake dates, and keep every lead moving in the CRM and EMR until it is scheduled or appropriately referred.
While I have not yet worked in a formal behavioral health admissions role, I have the combination of relevant experience, systems comfort, independent remote work habits, and genuine commitment to this population that the position requires. I am ready to learn the specific nuances of your programs, screening process, and Kipu (or equivalent) systems quickly, and I am already comfortable operating with the level of ownership this remote role demands.
I would welcome the chance to be the first voice someone hears on their path to healing. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to the work of Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.
Warmly, Jaylin N. Shepherd

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. candidates.cover_letter:
I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. As someone with experience in behavioral health, a background in psychology, and a current graduate student pursuing a Master of Arts in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, I understand how important it is for people to feel supported when they are trying to access care. What stood out to me about this position is the opportunity to be that first point of contact for individuals and families who may be overwhelmed, uncertain, or simply unsure of where to begin.

My previous experience working as a Behavioral Health Technician in a mental health and substance use treatment setting gave me valuable insight into the importance of compassionate communication, consistency, and creating an environment where people feel respected rather than judged. I have also worked as a Behavior Interventionist with students who have behavioral and emotional needs. These experiences have taught me to look beyond what someone may be expressing on the surface, remain patient in difficult moments, and approach each person with understanding. I believe those qualities are especially important when speaking with a parent who is concerned about their teenager or an individual who is taking the first step toward treatment.

In addition to my direct experience, my education has strengthened my understanding of mental health, human behavior, trauma, and the different circumstances that can affect a person’s willingness or ability to seek help. I earned my bachelor’s degree in Psychology from Southern University and A&M College and am continuing my education in Clinical Mental Health Counseling at The Chicago School. My long-term goal is to help make mental health support more accessible and to contribute to environments where individuals and families feel comfortable asking for help. I see this position as an opportunity to put that commitment into practice by helping people navigate the admissions process with clarity, professionalism, and compassion.

I also understand that providing good support means being dependable behind the scenes. My experience in behavioral health has exposed me to clinical documentation and electronic health record systems, including KIPU. I recognize the importance of accurate records, confidentiality, timely communication, and following through on responsibilities. I would bring an organized, attentive, and proactive approach to coordinating inquiries, communicating with families and referral sources, and helping prospective clients understand their next steps. I would also approach insurance verification, scheduling, and other admissions responsibilities with care, knowing that these details can make a real difference in how smoothly someone accesses treatment.

What I would bring to your team is more than an interest in mental health. I bring a genuine appreciation for the people behind every inquiry, along with a willingness to learn, take responsibility, and contribute to a team that helps individuals find the care they need. I would value the opportunity to support both adolescent mental health services and substance use treatment while helping create a welcoming, reassuring experience from the very first conversation.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my behavioral health experience, educational background, and commitment to compassionate care could contribute to your admissions team.

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

Howdy! I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy because this role reflects the kind of work I have spent years doing: showing up for people when they are struggling, building trust when trust does not come easily, and helping individuals feel supported without judgment.
I bring more than seven years of direct behavioral health experience working with children, adolescents, adults, and older adults facing complex mental health, behavioral, and co-occurring substance use challenges. At Promises Behavioral Health, I supported adults ages 18 to 81 in residential and partial hospitalization settings. My work required constant observation, strong boundaries, de-escalation, crisis response, accurate documentation working with Kipu, teamwork with clinicians, and—perhaps most importantly—the ability to connect with people who were overwhelmed, guarded, resistant, or simply having a very difficult day.
Before that, at Halifax Behavioral Health, I worked with at-risk children and adolescents ages 4 to 17. That experience taught me how much can be communicated without words and how important consistency, patience, calmness, and genuine human connection are when someone does not yet feel safe enough to engage.
Those same lessons have followed me throughout nearly three decades of equine work. Through my current business, Healed By The Horse, I create individualized experiences centered on trust, emotional awareness, regulation, confidence, and connection. Horses have reinforced something I already knew from behavioral health: you cannot force trust. You earn it by being present, observant, consistent, and authentic.
That is what draws me to remote work with Adolescent Wellness Academy.
I understand that meaningful mental health is not achieved by treating a diagnosis while overlooking the person living with it. People need to know that someone sees them, hears them, respects their experience, and will continue showing up. I would bring that mindset—along with substantial hands-on behavioral health experience, strong observational skills, compassion, professional boundaries, and a steady presence—to the Virtual Admissions Coordinator role.
I am also comfortable working independently, communicating virtually, documenting electronically via Kipu, learning new systems, and collaborating closely with multidisciplinary care teams. The opportunity to provide meaningful support within a virtual treatment environment is especially appealing to me.
I would be proud to bring my experience, patience, intuition, and very genuine commitment to helping people to Adolescent Wellness Academy. 

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to speak with you about how I could contribute to your team and, most importantly, to the individuals you serve.

Warmly,

Kris Secor

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a Bachelor of Social Work from UNC Charlotte, experience supporting intake and administrative operations within a college counseling center, and recent healthcare call center experience, I bring a strong combination of behavioral health knowledge, compassionate communication, and high-volume client support that aligns well with this role.

During my time with the Counseling Center at Onondaga Community College, I assisted with intake processes, answered phones, supported office administration, and interacted with individuals seeking counseling services. This experience strengthened my ability to communicate with empathy and professionalism while handling sensitive information and helping people navigate the first steps toward receiving support.

Most recently, I worked in healthcare customer service supporting hospital patient accounts. In this role, I managed approximately 50–60 calls per day and worked with systems including EPIC, MyChart, Artiva, and TCN. I regularly helped patients understand complex healthcare information, navigate stressful situations, and identify appropriate next steps. Working with individuals who were frustrated, overwhelmed, or uncertain taught me how important it is to remain calm, listen carefully, and make people feel heard while still moving the conversation toward a resolution.

My social work education has given me a strong understanding of person-centered care, mental health, crisis awareness, professional boundaries, and the importance of meeting individuals and families with compassion rather than judgment. I am particularly interested in bringing these skills into an admissions role where I can help adolescents and their families navigate what can be an overwhelming process and connect with appropriate mental health and substance use treatment.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my social work background, healthcare experience, and communication skills to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience could support your admissions team and the families you serve.

Sincerely,

Alyssa DiVeronica

candidates.cover_letter:
I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a bachelor's degree in Sociology, a concentration in Inequalities and Social Justice, and a professional background in client relations, human resources, and administrative coordination, I am eager to bring my communication skills and passion for helping others to a role where I can make a meaningful difference.

Throughout my professional experience, I have developed strong skills in building relationships, managing sensitive information, coordinating processes, and communicating with individuals from a variety of backgrounds. My experience in recruiting and human resources has strengthened my ability to approach conversations with empathy, ask thoughtful questions, and guide individuals through unfamiliar processes. In my current role as an Account Executive, I regularly manage client communications, coordinate next steps, and maintain consistent follow-through to ensure individuals feel informed and supported.

Beyond my professional experience, my academic background and previous volunteer work within the foster care system have shaped my interest in supporting individuals and families navigating difficult circumstances. I understand the importance of approaching sensitive situations without judgment and recognizing that every individual deserves to be treated with patience, dignity, and compassion. I see every day as an opportunity to make meaningful change in the lives of others.

What particularly draws me to this opportunity is the chance to be a reassuring first point of contact for individuals seeking mental health or substance use treatment. As someone who experienced particularly difficult teenage years without a support system, I find it incredibly fulfilling to support others who find themselves in the same position. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my organizational skills, attention to detail, and genuine desire to help others to your admissions team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would love the opportunity to further discuss how I could be an asset to your team and support the well-being of the young people across the state.

Sincerely,
Karolyn Bodwell

candidates.cover_letter:
Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a background in psychology, behavioral health, crisis support, and working directly with children and families, I was immediately drawn to this opportunity because of the importance you place on making the first point of contact compassionate, supportive, and clear.

Throughout my experience in behavioral health, I have learned that the way someone is treated during their first interaction can significantly affect whether they feel comfortable accepting help. In my work as a Behavioral Therapist/RBT, I have provided individualized behavioral support to children, communicated closely with parents and caregivers, maintained confidential documentation, assisted with scheduling and insurance coordination, and supported families through challenging behavioral situations. This experience has required patience, organization, professionalism, and the ability to communicate complicated information in a way that families can easily understand.

My crisis-support experience has strengthened these skills even further. As a Youth Crisis Counselor and Suicide Prevention Crisis Line Volunteer, I supported individuals during highly emotional and vulnerable moments through active listening, crisis intervention, risk and safety assessment, de-escalation, and connection to appropriate resources. These experiences taught me how to remain calm when someone on the other end of the conversation may be scared, overwhelmed, frustrated, or unsure of what to do next.

I also understand that effective admissions coordination requires more than compassion. It requires strong follow-through. My professional experience includes scheduling, insurance coordination, detailed documentation, maintaining confidentiality, communicating with families, and independently managing responsibilities. I am comfortable working with technology and learning new systems, and I understand the importance of accurate, timely, and HIPAA-compliant documentation when working in behavioral health.

I am especially interested in this position because it combines the administrative side of behavioral healthcare with direct human connection. I would value the opportunity to help a parent searching for treatment for their teenager, an individual seeking help for substance use or mental health concerns, or a provider trying to connect someone with an appropriate level of care. Even when a program is not the right fit, I believe every person deserves to leave that interaction feeling heard, respected, and clearer about what they can do next.

I would be grateful for the opportunity to bring my behavioral health experience, crisis-support background, communication skills, and commitment to compassionate care to your admissions team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Sincerely,

Brianna Otero
